title: Molecular basis of UV lesion binding and repair inhibition by ETS-family transcription factors
authors: Smitha Sivapragasam; J. Ross Terrell; Markus W. Germann; Marian F. Laughery; Michaela E. Everly; Shiva P. Adhikari; Patrick J. Hrdlicka; John J. Wyrick; Gregory M. K. Poon
one_liner_zh: 该文通过晶体结构和热力学研究ETS转录因子与UV损伤DNA（CPD）的结合及修复抑制机制，聚焦TF-DNA互作但以实验为主，缺乏AI或物理模拟方法，故评7分。
abstract: Mutation hotspots in melanoma frequently occur at DNA binding sites of ETS-family transcription factors, as ETS factors stimulate the formation of UV-induced cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers (CPDs) while suppressing repair at ETS-bound DNA sites. To elucidate the molecular mechanism by which ETS factors bind to damaged DNA sites and inhibit repair, we investigated the binding of members from the three major classes of the ETS superfamily (Ets1, ELF1 and PU.1) to cognate DNA containing a cis-syn TpT CPD. These site-specific CPDs modulated ETS recognition and repair by a model repair enzyme in a position-dependent manner, with a deaminated CPD located in a damage hotspot in the ETS binding motif consistently stimulating binding and repair inhibition by all three paralogs. Co-crystal structures of PU.1 reveal that CPDs and mismatches are recognized within the framework of canonical ETS/DNA complexes, but with highly differentiated thermodynamic and dynamic properties. Specifically, the CPD-bound complex exhibits unique dynamics that reveal a novel DNA-binding mode as well as inform how ETS domains navigate the DNA conformational landscape to predispose CPD induction. The results offer a molecular rationale for how ETS factors induce mutation hotspots in skin cancers and other UV-exposed tissues by promoting CPD induction and inhibiting repair. KEY POINTS ETS-family proteins from all major classes bind CPD-containing DNA sites. Engagement of CPD by ETS proteins inhibits DNA repair in a position-dependent manner. Structure and thermodynamics of ETS binding to damaged DNA differ from undamaged substrates.
abstract_zh: 黑色素瘤中的突变热点频繁出现在ETS家族转录因子的DNA结合位点，因为ETS因子刺激紫外线诱导的环丁烷嘧啶二聚体（CPDs）形成，同时抑制ETS结合DNA位点的修复。为阐明ETS因子结合受损DNA位点并抑制修复的分子机制，我们研究了ETS超家族三个主要类别成员（Ets1、ELF1和PU.1）与含有顺式-syn TpT CPD的认知DNA的结合。这些位点特异性CPD以位置依赖性方式调节ETS识别及模型修复酶的修复作用，其中位于ETS结合基序损伤热点中的脱氨基CPD持续刺激所有三种旁系同源物的结合和修复抑制。PU.1的共晶结构揭示，CPD和错配在经典ETS/DNA复合物框架内被识别，但具有高度分化的热力学和动力学特性。具体而言，CPD结合复合物表现出独特动力学，揭示了一种新型DNA结合模式，并阐明了ETS结构域如何导航DNA构象景观以易化CPD诱导。这些结果为ETS因子如何通过促进CPD诱导和抑制修复在皮肤癌及其他紫外线暴露组织中产生突变热点提供了分子层面的解释。要点 ETS家族蛋白的所有主要类别均能结合含CPD的DNA位点。ETS蛋白对CPD的参与以位置依赖性方式抑制DNA修复。ETS与受损DNA结合的结构和热力学特性不同于未受损底物。
